similarities.summary: Distributions share 78.5% overlap across the p10-p90 range (≥40% threshold). Jezero Crater floor regolith and fractured bedrock blockiness (5.0-17.5% area, median 10.8%) closely tracks Atacama desert pavement (4.5-15.2%, median 9.5%). Rover hazard-avoidance geometry is directly comparable.

candidate_stats.source: Atacama Desert Pavement Surface Rock Fraction Photogrammetry

target_stats.source: Perseverance Rover Navcam/Hazcam Boulder Surveys (Golombek et al. 2021)

similarities.direction_note: Rock hazard frequency curves match within 1.6% median offset.

similarities.summary: Shared aqueous alteration mineral suite: Perseverance SuperCam and CRISM detect Fe/Mg-smectite phyllosilicates, hydrated sulfates, and carbonate minerals in Jezero paleolake deposits. Atacama salar basins display an identical mineral paragenesis: smectite clays and hydrated calcium sulfates (gypsum CaSO₄·2H₂O) formed via evaporating standing bodies of water.
similarities.direction_note: Paleolake evaporite and smectite clay alteration suites are directly analogous.
similarities.detail: CRISM hyperspectral absorption bands align with Atacama salar clay-sulfate spectra.

mismatches.summary: Earth Atacama shows aeolian deflation and trace evaporite alteration (gypsum, halite). Target surface has no atmospheric weathering — only micrometeorite comminution (Moon) or aeolian perchlorate chemistry (Mars). Earth soil is weathered; target regolith is pristine or reactive.

mismatches.summary: Distributions share 0.0% overlap (completely disjoint). Perseverance MEDA measures massive diurnal swings of 76-92 K at Jezero due to rapid radiative cooling through the thin 6 hPa CO₂ atmosphere. Atacama diurnal swings are buffered to 22-36 K.

candidate_stats.source: Atacama Annual Diurnal Temperature Swing (Max - Min)

target_stats.source: Perseverance MEDA Diurnal Surface Thermal Amplitude

mismatches.direction_note: Martian diurnal thermal swing is ~3x wider than Earth desert swing.

mismatches.summary: Direct cross-body temperature comparison is subject to fundamental atmospheric physics disparity: Earth has a 1,013 hPa convective boundary layer; Mars has ~6 hPa CO₂ with weak convective coupling; Moon is hard vacuum (~10⁻¹² hPa) with purely radiative heat transfer.

similarities.summary: Distributions overlap 66.7% across the p10-p90 range. Mars Jezero experiences an annual daylight fraction of ~0.50, operationally matching Atacama's ~0.51 daylight fraction.

candidate_stats.source: Analytical Spherical Astronomy & Atacama Clear-Sky Solar Geometry

target_stats.source: Mars Climate Database & Orbital Insolation Model (Jezero 18.4°N)

similarities.direction_note: Diurnal daylight fractions match within 1.0% operational tolerance.

similarities.summary: Earth diurnal cycle (24.00h) closely matches Mars sol (24.66h). Operational day/night cadence, crew circadian scheduling, and solar battery charge/discharge cycles are directly analogous (offset: +39.6 min/sol).
similarities.direction_note: Mars sol is 39m 35s longer than Earth day (within 2.7% delta).

mismatches.summary: Solar constant at Mars is ~590 W/m² (~43% of Earth's 1361 W/m²). Surface solar irradiance peak at Jezero reaches ~450-550 W/m² under clear sky, compared to 1,050-1,250 W/m² at high-elevation Atacama. Solar arrays on Mars require >2.2x collector area for equivalent power output.
mismatches.direction_note: Earth solar flux is ~2.3x higher due to 1/r² orbital distance offset.

uncertainties: Resolution disparity is the dominant uncertainty: candidate at 29 m/px captures sub-km terrain; target at 14.8 km/px averages landscape-scale features.
Target grid (10×10 = 100 pixels) is too coarse for distribution comparison. Summary statistics used as reference bounds.
Thermal and surface rock evaluations reflect LRO Diviner polar radiometry and Mars 2020 MEDA / TES records; seasonal subsurface heat conduction models remain pending.
Geological crosswalk is a draft built from map group names only. Full unit descriptions have not been verified.
Mars solar irradiance is modeled under mean atmospheric optical depth (tau=0.5); local dust storm events cause significant transient flux attenuation.

limitations.impact: Slope stability, avalanche dynamics, and rover traction differ fundamentally. Equal slope angles are NOT equally hazardous across bodies.
No convective heat dissipation, no liquid water stability, no atmospheric pressure on suits or habitats.

limitations.target: Elevated UV and cosmic-ray flux; thin CO₂ atmosphere offers minimal shielding
limitations.impact: Surface habitats require regolith berming or sub-surface siting. No Earth analogue preparation addresses this.

limitations.earth: Active microbial, hydro-chemical, and aeolian weathering
limitations.target: Aeolian dust transport; toxic perchlorate (ClO₄⁻) chemistry; no liquid water
limitations.impact: Earth regolith contains organic binders. Target body regolith is mechanically abrasive or chemically hazardous.
